```python
class EnsembleSolution(BaseModel):
    """
    A complete ensemble solution with statistics and predictions.

    Represents a single ensemble of parameter sets, containing the ensemble
    composition, parameter statistics, model predictions with confidence
    intervals, and performance metrics.

    Attributes
    ----------
    ensemble_size : int
        Number of parameter sets in this ensemble
    selected_indices : list[int]
        Indices of parameter sets selected for this ensemble
    ensemble_parameters : list[dict[str, float]]
        List of parameter dictionaries in this ensemble
    parameter_statistics : dict[str, ParameterSetStatistics]
        Statistics for each parameter across the ensemble
    prediction_positions : list[float]
        Positions on the axis of the prediction series, ascending: the unit
        grid up to one past the last observation, and every observation
        position and window start
    prediction_median : dict[str, list[float]]
        Median prediction of each output, one value per position
    prediction_ci_lower : dict[str, list[float]]
        Lower bound of the confidence interval of each output, per position
    prediction_ci_upper : dict[str, list[float]]
        Upper bound of the confidence interval of each output, per position
    windowed_prediction_positions : dict[str, list[float]]
        Positions the windowed values are taken at, one per windowed observation
    coverage_percentage : float
        Percentage of observed data points within the confidence intervals
    average_ci_width : float
        Average width of confidence intervals across time and compartments
    ci_width : float
        Mean observed-data interval width normalized by observation magnitude.
    coverage : float
        Normalized coverage objective [0, 1] used in optimization
    point_parameters : dict[str, float]
        Parameters of the lowest-loss selected member. This is the only
        parameter dictionary suitable for constructing a single point model.
    point_loss : float
        Calibration loss of point_parameters.
    central_loss : float
        The memberwise-median prediction scored with the problem's loss function
        (the same loss the members were fit with), comparable to point_loss.
    observation_diagnostics : dict[str, dict[str, float]]
        Per-observation-series coverage and interval-width diagnostics.
    selection_diagnostics : dict[str, float]
        Candidate-search diagnostics produced by the selected backend.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    ensemble_size: int = Field(description="Number of parameter sets in this ensemble")
    selected_indices: list[int] = Field(
        description="Indices of selected parameter sets"
    )
    ensemble_parameters: list[dict[str, float]] = Field(
        description="List of parameter dictionaries in this ensemble"
    )
    parameter_statistics: dict[str, ParameterSetStatistics] = Field(
        description="Statistics for each parameter across the ensemble"
    )
    prediction_positions: list[float] = Field(
        description="Positions on the axis of the prediction series, ascending"
    )
    prediction_median: dict[str, list[float]] = Field(
        description="Median prediction of each output, one value per position"
    )
    prediction_ci_lower: dict[str, list[float]] = Field(
        description="Lower confidence bound of each output, one value per position"
    )
    prediction_ci_upper: dict[str, list[float]] = Field(
        description="Upper confidence bound of each output, one value per position"
    )
    windowed_prediction_positions: dict[str, list[float]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description=(
            "Positions the windowed values are taken at, one entry per windowed "
            "observation of the output, sorted by position"
        ),
    )
    windowed_prediction_median: dict[str, list[float]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Correct windowed median for outputs with windowed observations",
    )
    windowed_prediction_ci_lower: dict[str, list[float]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Correct windowed lower CI for outputs with windowed observations",
    )
    windowed_prediction_ci_upper: dict[str, list[float]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Correct windowed upper CI for outputs with windowed observations",
    )
    coverage_percentage: float = Field(
        description="Percentage of observed data points within confidence intervals"
    )
    average_ci_width: float = Field(description="Average width of confidence intervals")
    ci_width: float = Field(
        description=(
            "Mean observed-data interval width normalized by observation magnitude"
        )
    )
    coverage: float = Field(description="Normalized coverage objective [0, 1]")
    point_parameters: dict[str, float] = Field(
        description="Parameters of the lowest-loss selected ensemble member"
    )
    point_loss: float = Field(description="Loss of the selected point member")
    central_loss: float = Field(
        description=(
            "Memberwise-median prediction scored with the problem's loss function"

    observation_diagnostics: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = Field(

        description="Coverage and interval diagnostics grouped by observation series",

    selection_diagnostics: dict[str, float] = Field(

        description="Ensemble selection diagnostics",
```

## ci_percentiles

```python
ci_percentiles(confidence_level: float) -> tuple[float, float]
```

Lower and upper percentile points of a two-sided confidence interval.

Parameters:

| Name               | Type    | Description                                                 | Default    |
| ------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `confidence_level` | `float` | Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1. | *required* |

Returns:

| Type                  | Description                                            |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `tuple[float, float]` | Lower and upper percentile points, on the 0-100 scale. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                          |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `ValueError` | If confidence_level is not strictly between 0 and 1. |

Source code in `commol/api/probabilistic/intervals.py`

```python
def ci_percentiles(confidence_level: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """
    Lower and upper percentile points of a two-sided confidence interval.

    Parameters
    ----------
    confidence_level : float
        Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[float, float]
        Lower and upper percentile points, on the 0-100 scale.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``confidence_level`` is not strictly between 0 and 1.
    """
    if not 0.0 < confidence_level < 1.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"confidence_level must be strictly between 0 and 1, got "
            f"{confidence_level}. Note this is a fraction, not a percentage: "
            f"use 0.95 for a 95% interval."
        )
    return (
        (1.0 - confidence_level) / 2.0 * 100.0,
        (1.0 + confidence_level) / 2.0 * 100.0,
    )
```


Spread of one quantity across the members of an ensemble.

Each member must already be reduced to the quantity of interest, so that the reported interval is a percentile of member values.

Parameters:

| Name               | Type              | Description                                                          | Default    |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `per_member`       | \`Sequence[float] | Sequence\[Sequence[float]\]                                          | NDArray\`  |
| `confidence_level` | `float`           | Confidence level of the reported interval, strictly between 0 and 1. | *required* |

Returns:

| Type               | Description                |
| ------------------ | -------------------------- |
| \`dict[str, float] | dict\[str, list[float]\]\` |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ValueError` | If confidence_level is out of range, or per_member is empty. |

Source code in `commol/api/probabilistic/intervals.py`

```python
def member_statistics(
    per_member: EnsembleValues,
    confidence_level: float,
) -> dict[str, float] | dict[str, list[float]] | dict[str, float | list[float]]:
    """
    Spread of one quantity across the members of an ensemble.

    Each member must already be reduced to the quantity of interest, so that
    the reported interval is a percentile of member values.

    Parameters
    ----------
    per_member : Sequence[float] | Sequence[Sequence[float]] | NDArray
        One entry per ensemble member. Entries may be scalars, in which case
        every returned statistic is a scalar, or equal-length series, in which
        case every returned statistic is a series reduced across members at
        each position. A numpy array is accepted, but its rank is not visible
        to a type checker; pass a list of lists for a precise return type.
    confidence_level : float
        Confidence level of the reported interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, float] | dict[str, list[float]]
        Keys ``mean``, ``median``, ``ci_lower``, ``ci_upper``, ``min`` and
        ``max``. Scalar members give scalar statistics, series members give
        series statistics.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``confidence_level`` is out of range, or ``per_member`` is empty.
    """
    lower_percentile, upper_percentile = ci_percentiles(confidence_level)
    values = np.asarray(per_member, dtype=float)
    if values.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("per_member must hold at least one ensemble member.")

    return {
        "mean": np.mean(values, axis=0).tolist(),
        "median": np.percentile(values, 50.0, axis=0).tolist(),
        "ci_lower": np.percentile(values, lower_percentile, axis=0).tolist(),
        "ci_upper": np.percentile(values, upper_percentile, axis=0).tolist(),
        "min": np.min(values, axis=0).tolist(),
        "max": np.max(values, axis=0).tolist(),
    }
```

# Reports API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

Plain-dictionary reports of a calibrated model and of a run. Guide: [Reports](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/reports/index.md).

## applied_parameters_report

```python
applied_parameters_report(model: Model, result: CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | Mapping[str, float], problem: CalibrationProblem | None = None, parameter_statistics: Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None = None, confidence_level: float | None = None) -> AppliedParametersReport
```

Report every parameter of a calibrated model, and the values of its kind.

Each entry carries the value the model holds and whether calibration set it, so entries the calibration left alone appear alongside the fitted ones. The structure of the model adds the sections of its kind (`ModelStructure.report_sections`); an aggregate model adds `initial_conditions`.

Parameters that are not a single number, such as a formula or a series, are omitted: they are inputs rather than fitted values. `factor` parameters have no place in the model, so they are reported from `problem` when it is given.

Initial conditions of an aggregate model carry the effective `value` the engine builds from the uniform expansion plus the declared compartment overrides, its `fraction` as that value over the declared total, and the `group` it belongs to: `total` for bins and unconditional stratifications, and the conditioning categories for a conditional one. The `total` row is the declared total, with fraction 1.0. A bin left uncalibrated keeps a `None` fraction and `None` value as its "needs calibration" marker even when overrides touch some of its compartments.

For a probabilistic result each entry gains an `interval` holding the ensemble spread. A parameter is in the unit it was calibrated in. An initial-condition entry is in the fraction the row reports: a conditional stratification's category is calibrated as a group fraction but reported over the total, so its interval is rescaled by the group's share of the total and brackets the reported fraction.

Parameters:

| Name                   | Type                                   | Description                            | Default                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`                | `Model`                                | The model carrying the applied values. | *required*                                                                                                          |
| `result`               | \`CalibrationResult                    | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult         | Mapping\`                                                                                                           |
| `problem`              | \`CalibrationProblem                   | None\`                                 | The problem the result came from, used to report factor parameters.                                                 |
| `parameter_statistics` | \`Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None\`                                 | Ensemble spread per entry. Taken from result when it is a probabilistic result and this is not given.               |
| `confidence_level`     | \`float                                | None\`                                 | Confidence level the intervals describe. Taken from result when it is a probabilistic result and this is not given. |

Returns:

| Type                      | Description                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AppliedParametersReport` | Key parameters and the sections of the kind (initial_conditions for an aggregate model), preceded by confidence_level when there is one. |

Source code in `commol/api/reporting.py`

```python
def applied_parameters_report(
    model: Model,
    result: CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | Mapping[str, float],
    problem: CalibrationProblem | None = None,
    parameter_statistics: Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None = None,
    confidence_level: float | None = None,
) -> AppliedParametersReport:
    """
    Report every parameter of a calibrated model, and the values of its kind.

    Each entry carries the value the model holds and whether calibration set
    it, so entries the calibration left alone appear alongside the fitted ones.
    The structure of the model adds the sections of its kind
    (`ModelStructure.report_sections`); an aggregate model adds
    ``initial_conditions``.

    Parameters that are not a single number, such as a formula or a
    series, are omitted: they are inputs rather than fitted values.
    ``factor`` parameters have no place in the model, so they are reported from
    `problem` when it is given.

    Initial conditions of an aggregate model carry the effective
    ``value`` the engine builds
    from the uniform expansion plus the declared compartment overrides, its
    ``fraction`` as that value over the declared total, and the
    ``group`` it belongs to: ``total`` for bins and unconditional
    stratifications, and the conditioning categories for a conditional one.
    The ``total`` row is the declared total, with fraction 1.0. A bin left
    uncalibrated keeps a ``None`` fraction and ``None`` value as its "needs
    calibration" marker even when overrides touch some of its compartments.

    For a probabilistic result each entry gains an ``interval`` holding the
    ensemble spread. A parameter is in the unit it was calibrated in. An
    initial-condition entry is in the fraction the row reports: a conditional
    stratification's category is calibrated as a group fraction but reported
    over the total, so its interval is rescaled by the group's share of the
    total and brackets the reported fraction.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : Model
        The model carrying the applied values.
    result : CalibrationResult | ProbabilisticCalibrationResult | Mapping
        The calibration outcome, or a mapping of parameter id to value such as
        one ensemble member's parameters.
    problem : CalibrationProblem | None, optional
        The problem the result came from, used to report factor parameters.
    parameter_statistics : Mapping[str, ParameterSetStatistics] | None, optional
        Ensemble spread per entry. Taken from `result` when it is a
        probabilistic result and this is not given.
    confidence_level : float | None, optional
        Confidence level the intervals describe. Taken from `result` when it is
        a probabilistic result and this is not given.

    Returns
    -------
    AppliedParametersReport
        Key ``parameters`` and the sections of the kind (``initial_conditions``
        for an aggregate model), preceded by ``confidence_level`` when there
        is one.
    """
    calibrated = calibrated_values(result)
    parameter_statistics, confidence_level = _ensemble_details(
        result, parameter_statistics, confidence_level
    )
    calibrated_ids = set(calibrated)

    parameters: dict[str, ParameterEntry] = {
        parameter.id: _parameter_entry(
            parameter.id, parameter.value, calibrated_ids, parameter_statistics
        )
        for parameter in model.parameters
        if isinstance(parameter.value, (int, float))
    }
    for factor_id in _factor_ids(problem):
        if factor_id in calibrated:
            parameters[factor_id] = _parameter_entry(
                factor_id, calibrated[factor_id], calibrated_ids, parameter_statistics
            )

    report: dict[str, object] = {}
    # `confidence_level` leads the report, so it is written first.
    if confidence_level is not None:
        report["confidence_level"] = confidence_level
    report["parameters"] = parameters
    report.update(
        model.structure.report_sections(model, calibrated_ids, parameter_statistics)
    )
    return cast(AppliedParametersReport, report)
```

## simulation_report

```python
simulation_report(simulation: Simulation, results: SimulationResults, at: Sequence[float], window: float, num_windows: int, observed_data: Iterable[ObservedDataPoint] = (), accumulators: Iterable[str] = (), ensemble_runs: Sequence[SimulationResults] | None = None, confidence_level: float | None = None) -> SimulationReport
```

Report the observed data, compartment series and accumulators of a run.

The three blocks share one window axis, so the observed values, the windowed accumulator increments and the sampled series can be read against each other. With `ensemble_runs` every leaf becomes a `{mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min, max}` block computed across members, and the layout is otherwise unchanged.

Callers add whatever envelope they need around these blocks, such as a run label, axis labels or domain-specific summary figures.

Parameters:

| Name               | Type                          | Description                                                      | Default                                     |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `simulation`       | `Simulation`                  | The simulation the results came from.                            | *required*                                  |
| `results`          | `SimulationResults`           | Results of a run, with their positions.                          | *required*                                  |
| `at`               | `Sequence[float]`             | Positions the series and cumulative accumulators are sampled at. | *required*                                  |
| `window`           | `float`                       | Length of one window on the axis.                                | *required*                                  |
| `num_windows`      | `int`                         | Number of windows on the observed and windowed axes.             | *required*                                  |
| `observed_data`    | `Iterable[ObservedDataPoint]` | The calibration targets to report alongside the run.             | `()`                                        |
| `accumulators`     | `Iterable[str]`               | Accumulator ids to report.                                       | `()`                                        |
| `ensemble_runs`    | \`Sequence[SimulationResults] | None\`                                                           | One results mapping per ensemble member.    |
| `confidence_level` | \`float                       | None\`                                                           | Confidence level of the reported intervals. |

Returns:

| Type               | Description                             |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| `SimulationReport` | Keys observed, series and accumulators. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ValueError` | If the results have no value at a position the report reads. |

Source code in `commol/api/reporting.py`

```python
def simulation_report(
    simulation: Simulation,
    results: SimulationResults,
    at: Sequence[float],
    window: float,
    num_windows: int,
    observed_data: Iterable[ObservedDataPoint] = (),
    accumulators: Iterable[str] = (),
    ensemble_runs: Sequence[SimulationResults] | None = None,
    confidence_level: float | None = None,
) -> SimulationReport:
    """
    Report the observed data, compartment series and accumulators of a run.

    The three blocks share one window axis, so the observed values, the
    windowed accumulator increments and the sampled series can be read against
    each other. With `ensemble_runs` every leaf becomes a
    ``{mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min, max}`` block computed across
    members, and the layout is otherwise unchanged.

    Callers add whatever envelope they need around these blocks, such as a run
    label, axis labels or domain-specific summary figures.

    Parameters
    ----------
    simulation : Simulation
        The simulation the results came from.
    results : SimulationResults
        Results of a run, with their positions.
    at : Sequence[float]
        Positions the series and cumulative accumulators are sampled at.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    num_windows : int
        Number of windows on the observed and windowed axes.
    observed_data : Iterable[ObservedDataPoint], optional
        The calibration targets to report alongside the run.
    accumulators : Iterable[str], optional
        Accumulator ids to report.
    ensemble_runs : Sequence[SimulationResults] | None, optional
        One results mapping per ensemble member.
    confidence_level : float | None, optional
        Confidence level of the reported intervals.

    Returns
    -------
    SimulationReport
        Keys ``observed``, ``series`` and ``accumulators``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the results have no value at a position the report reads.
    """
    accumulator_ids = list(accumulators)
    return {
        "observed": observed_report(observed_data, window, num_windows),
        "series": series_report(
            simulation,
            results,
            at,
            accumulator_ids,
            ensemble_runs,
            confidence_level,
        ),
        "accumulators": accumulators_report(
            simulation,
            results,
            accumulator_ids,
            at,
            window,
            num_windows,
            ensemble_runs,
            confidence_level,
        ),
    }
```

# Simulation API

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

Runs a model and reads its outputs. Guide: [Running Simulations](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/guide/simulations/index.md).

## Simulation

A Facade for running a simulation from a defined Model.

The engine follows the model: `run` and `engine` rebuild it when `model_definition` no longer serializes to the JSON the engine was built from, for example after `Model.update_parameters`.

Source code in `commol/api/simulation.py`

```python
class Simulation:
    """
    A Facade for running a simulation from a defined Model.

    The engine follows the model: ``run`` and ``engine`` rebuild it when
    ``model_definition`` no longer serializes to the JSON the engine was built
    from, for example after ``Model.update_parameters``.
    """

    def __init__(self, model: Model):
        """
        Initializes the simulation engine from a Pydantic Model definition.

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            A fully constructed and validated model object, of any kind.
            None values for parameters/initial conditions if used for calibration.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If the structure of the model is not a `ModelStructure`.

        """
        if not isinstance(model.structure, ModelStructure):
            raise TypeError(
                f"The structure of model '{model.name}' is a "
                f"{type(model.structure).__name__}, not a ModelStructure. A model "
                "holds the structure of its kind, such as an Aggregate."
            )
        logging.info(f"Initializing Simulation with model: '{model.name}'")
        self.model_definition: Model = model
        self._build_engine(model.model_dump_json())

    def _build_engine(self, model_json: str) -> None:
        """Build the engine and its output names from a model JSON."""
        self._model_json: str = model_json
        self._engine: "EngineProtocol" = build_engine(model_json)
        self._simulation_outputs: list[str] = self._engine.output_names
        logging.info(
            f"Simulation engine ready. Outputs: {len(self._simulation_outputs)}"
        )

    def _sync_engine(self) -> None:
        """Rebuild the engine when the model changed since it was built."""
        model_json = self.model_definition.model_dump_json()
        if model_json != self._model_json:
            logging.info("Model changed since the engine was built; rebuilding it.")
            self._build_engine(model_json)

    def _validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self, model: Model) -> None:
        """
        Validates that every parameter, and every value of the model kind, has
        a value (is calibrated).

        Parameters
        ----------
        model : Model
            The model to validate.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If any parameter, or any value of the model kind such as an
            initial condition, has a None value.
        """
        uncalibrated_params = model.get_uncalibrated_parameters()
        uncalibrated_ics = model.structure.uncalibrated_values()

        errors = []
        if uncalibrated_params:
            errors.append(
                f"Parameters requiring calibration: {', '.join(uncalibrated_params)}"
            )
        if uncalibrated_ics:
            errors.append(
                f"Initial conditions requiring calibration: "
                f"{', '.join(uncalibrated_ics)}"
            )

        if errors:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cannot run Simulation: {'; '.join(errors)}. "
                f"Please calibrate these values before running a simulation."
            )

    @property
    def is_stochastic(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the engine of the model draws random numbers."""
        return commol_rs.engine.EngineType(
            self.model_definition.engine.type
        ).is_stochastic

    def _seed_run(self, seed: int | None) -> int | None:
        """Seed the engine of a stochastic model; None for a deterministic one."""
        if not self.is_stochastic:
            return None
        seed = draw_seed() if seed is None else check_seed(seed)
        self._engine.set_seed(seed)
        return seed

    def run(self, num_steps: int, *, seed: int | None = None) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        Runs the simulation from the initial state on its default grid.

        Every call starts at position 0 with the current ``model_definition``,
        so two calls with the same model, and the same seed for a stochastic
        engine, give the same result. To continue a run, call
        ``simulation.engine.step()``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        num_steps : int
            The number of steps: the results hold the positions
            ``0, 1, ..., num_steps``.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of a stochastic engine, a whole number from 0 to
            ``2**64 - 1``. None draws one, which ``results.seed`` keeps, so
            every run can be repeated. A deterministic engine ignores it.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One value per position for each output, the positions, and the
            seed of a stochastic run.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a step leaves an amount below zero; the message names the
            compartment, the step and the flows out of it.
        ValueError
            If a parameter or initial condition has no value, or the seed is
            not a whole number from 0 to ``2**64 - 1``.
        """
        self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
        self._sync_engine()
        used_seed = self._seed_run(seed)
        self._engine.reset()
        logging.info(f"Running simulation for {num_steps} steps.")
        start = time.time()
        positions, rows = self._engine.run(num_steps)
        logging.info(f"Simulation complete. It took {time.time() - start} seconds.")
        return SimulationResults.from_rows(
            positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows, seed=used_seed
        )

    def run_at(
        self, at: Sequence[float], *, seed: int | None = None
    ) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        Runs the simulation from the initial state and reports at given positions.

        The positions are on the axis, the independent variable of the model.
        The engine decides which positions its model type reports at: a
        DifferentialEquations model at any finite, non-negative position, from
        the dense output of its solver; a DifferenceEquations model only at
        integer steps.

        Parameters
        ----------
        at : Sequence[float]
            Sorted, unique positions to report at.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of a stochastic engine; see `run`.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One value per position for each output, the positions, and the
            seed of a stochastic run.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a step leaves an amount below zero; the message names the
            compartment, the step and the flows out of it.
        ValueError
            If a parameter or initial condition has no value, the positions are
            not sorted and unique, or the engine does not report at one of them;
            the message is the engine's.
        """
        positions = [float(position) for position in at]
        self._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(self.model_definition)
        self._sync_engine()
        used_seed = self._seed_run(seed)
        self._engine.reset()
        rows = self._engine.run_at(positions)
        return SimulationResults.from_rows(
            positions, self._simulation_outputs, rows, seed=used_seed
        )

    def replicates(self, n: int, *, seed: int | None = None) -> "ReplicateRuns":
        """
        Replicates of the runs of a stochastic engine.

        The returned object has ``run`` and ``run_at``, as `Simulation`, and
        they return `SimulationReplicates`: ``n`` runs, each with its own seed,
        run in parallel in the engine. Replicate ``i`` takes the seed derived
        from ``seed`` and ``i`` (the SplitMix64 of ``seed + i``), so it gives
        the same run however many replicates run.

        Parameters
        ----------
        n : int
            How many replicates, at least 1.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed the replicate seeds derive from, a whole number from 0 to
            ``2**64 - 1``. None draws one, which the replicates keep.

        Returns
        -------
        ReplicateRuns
            The runner of the replicates.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the engine is deterministic (every replicate would be equal),
            ``n`` is below 1, or the seed is not valid.
        """
        if not self.is_stochastic:
            raise ValueError(
                f"The {self.model_definition.engine.type} engine is deterministic: "
                "every replicate would be equal. Replicates need a stochastic engine."
            )
        if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int) or n < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"The number of replicates is at least 1, got {n!r}.")
        return ReplicateRuns(self, n, draw_seed() if seed is None else check_seed(seed))

    @property
    def engine(self) -> "EngineProtocol":
        """
        The engine for the current ``model_definition``.

        It is rebuilt, at step 0, when the model changed since it was built.
        Otherwise it is the same object, in the state the last ``run`` or
        ``step`` left it.
        """
        self._sync_engine()
        return self._engine

    @property
    def simulation_outputs(self) -> list[str]:
        """Names of the columns returned by simulation runs."""
        self._sync_engine()
        return self._simulation_outputs

    def outputs_for(self, id: str) -> list[str]:
        """
        Names of the outputs a source id expands into.

        The structure of the model groups its outputs by source
        (`ModelStructure.outputs_by_source`): for an aggregate model, by
        bin and accumulator.

        Parameters
        ----------
        id : str
            A source id, such as a bin id or an accumulator id.

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            Output names for that id, in the order the engine reports them.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If `id` is not a source of the model.
        """
        model = self.model_definition
        outputs = model.structure.outputs_by_source(model)
        if id not in outputs:
            raise KeyError(
                f"'{id}' is not a bin or accumulator of model "
                f"'{self.model_definition.name}'. Available: {sorted(outputs)}"
            )
        return outputs[id]

    def group_outputs(self, ids: Iterable[str]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
        """
        Group output names by the bin or accumulator they belong to.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Bin and accumulator ids.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[str]]
            Each id mapped to its output names, keeping the order given.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model.
        """
        return {id: self.outputs_for(id) for id in ids}

    def total_series(
        self,
        results: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
        ids: Iterable[str],
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Sum the outputs of the given bins or accumulators at each position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        results : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]
            Simulation results, such as those of `run` or `run_at`.
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Bin and accumulator ids whose outputs are summed together.

        Returns
        -------
        list[float]
            One value per position of `results`.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
            output is missing from `results`.
        """
        names = [name for id in ids for name in self.outputs_for(id)]
        missing = [name for name in names if name not in results]
        if missing:
            raise KeyError(f"Missing output series in results: {sorted(missing)}")
        if not names:
            return []
        return [
            sum(values)
            for values in zip(*(results[name] for name in names), strict=True)
        ]

    def windowed_totals(
        self,
        results: SimulationResults,
        ids: Iterable[str],
        window: float,
        at: Iterable[float] | None = None,
    ) -> list[float]:
        """
        Amount the given accumulators gained over each window.

        Parameters
        ----------
        results : SimulationResults
            Simulation results, with their positions.
        ids : Iterable[str]
            Accumulator ids whose outputs are summed before windowing.
        window : float
            Length of one window on the axis.
        at : Iterable[float] | None, optional
            Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete
            window of the results (:func:`commol.window_ends`). Pass the
            observation positions to reproduce exactly the values a
            calibration used.

        Returns
        -------
        list[float]
            One increment per window.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
            output is missing from `results`.
        ValueError
            If `window` is not positive, or the results have no value at the
            end or the start of a requested window.
        """
        return windowed_totals(
            self.total_series(results, ids), results.positions, window, at
        )
```


Initializes the simulation engine from a Pydantic Model definition.

Parameters:

| Name    | Type    | Description                                                                                                                         | Default    |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `model` | `Model` | A fully constructed and validated model object, of any kind. None values for parameters/initial conditions if used for calibration. | *required* |

Raises:

| Type        | Description                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `TypeError` | If the structure of the model is not a ModelStructure. |

Source code in `commol/api/simulation.py`

```python
def __init__(self, model: Model):
    """
    Initializes the simulation engine from a Pydantic Model definition.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : Model
        A fully constructed and validated model object, of any kind.
        None values for parameters/initial conditions if used for calibration.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the structure of the model is not a `ModelStructure`.

    """
    if not isinstance(model.structure, ModelStructure):
        raise TypeError(
            f"The structure of model '{model.name}' is a "
            f"{type(model.structure).__name__}, not a ModelStructure. A model "
            "holds the structure of its kind, such as an Aggregate."
        )
    logging.info(f"Initializing Simulation with model: '{model.name}'")
    self.model_definition: Model = model
    self._build_engine(model.model_dump_json())
```

```python
total_series(results: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]], ids: Iterable[str]) -> list[float]
```

Sum the outputs of the given bins or accumulators at each position.

| `ids`     | `Iterable[str]`                 | Bin and accumulator ids whose outputs are summed together. | *required* |

| Type          | Description                        |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `list[float]` | One value per position of results. |

Source code in `commol/api/simulation.py`

```python
def total_series(
    self,
    results: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
    ids: Iterable[str],
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Sum the outputs of the given bins or accumulators at each position.

    Parameters
    ----------
    results : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]
        Simulation results, such as those of `run` or `run_at`.
    ids : Iterable[str]
        Bin and accumulator ids whose outputs are summed together.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One value per position of `results`.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
        output is missing from `results`.
    """
    names = [name for id in ids for name in self.outputs_for(id)]
    missing = [name for name in names if name not in results]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(f"Missing output series in results: {sorted(missing)}")
    if not names:
        return []
    return [
        sum(values)
        for values in zip(*(results[name] for name in names), strict=True)
    ]
```

#### windowed_totals

```python
windowed_totals(results: SimulationResults, ids: Iterable[str], window: float, at: Iterable[float] | None = None) -> list[float]
```

Amount the given accumulators gained over each window.

| Type         | Description                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `KeyError`   | If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected output is missing from results.      |
| `ValueError` | If window is not positive, or the results have no value at the end or the start of a requested window. |

Source code in `commol/api/simulation.py`

```python
def windowed_totals(
    self,
    results: SimulationResults,
    ids: Iterable[str],
    window: float,
    at: Iterable[float] | None = None,
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Amount the given accumulators gained over each window.

    Parameters
    ----------
    results : SimulationResults
        Simulation results, with their positions.
    ids : Iterable[str]
        Accumulator ids whose outputs are summed before windowing.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    at : Iterable[float] | None, optional
        Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete
        window of the results (:func:`commol.window_ends`). Pass the
        observation positions to reproduce exactly the values a
        calibration used.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One increment per window.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If an id is not a bin or accumulator of the model, or an expected
        output is missing from `results`.
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive, or the results have no value at the
        end or the start of a requested window.
    """
    return windowed_totals(
        self.total_series(results, ids), results.positions, window, at
    )
```

## SimulationResults

Bases: `dict[str, list[float]]`

Values of every output at each position on the axis.

A `dict` from output name to one value per position, so `results["A"]`, `json.dumps(results)` and `pandas.DataFrame(results)` work as for any mapping. The positions the values were read at are in :attr:`positions`.

Attributes:

| Name        | Type          | Description                                                                              |
| ----------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `positions` | `list[float]` | Positions on the axis, ascending. results[name][i] is the value of name at positions[i]. |
| `seed`      | \`int         | None\`                                                                                   |

Source code in `commol/api/results.py`

```python
class SimulationResults(dict[str, list[float]]):
    """
    Values of every output at each position on the axis.

    A ``dict`` from output name to one value per position, so
    ``results["A"]``, ``json.dumps(results)`` and
    ``pandas.DataFrame(results)`` work as for any mapping. The positions the
    values were read at are in :attr:`positions`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    positions : list[float]
        Positions on the axis, ascending. ``results[name][i]`` is the value of
        ``name`` at ``positions[i]``.
    seed : int | None
        The seed of the run of a stochastic engine, which repeats it; None for
        a deterministic engine, whose runs depend on no seed.
    """

    positions: list[float]
    seed: int | None

    def __init__(
        self,
        positions: Iterable[float],
        values: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | None = None,
        seed: int | None = None,
    ):
        """
        Results at the given positions.

        Parameters
        ----------
        positions : Iterable[float]
            Positions on the axis, ascending.
        values : Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | None, optional
            One value per position for each output.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of the run, or None when it depends on no seed.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an output does not have one value per position.
        """
        super().__init__(
            {name: list(series) for name, series in (values or {}).items()}
        )
        self.positions = [float(position) for position in positions]
        self.seed = seed
        for name, series in self.items():
            if len(series) != len(self.positions):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Output '{name}' has {len(series)} values for "
                    f"{len(self.positions)} positions."
                )

    @classmethod
    def from_rows(
        cls,
        positions: Sequence[float],
        names: Sequence[str],
        rows: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
        seed: int | None = None,
    ) -> "SimulationResults":
        """
        Results from one row of output values per position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        positions : Sequence[float]
            Positions on the axis, ascending.
        names : Sequence[str]
            Output names, in the order of each row.
        rows : Sequence[Sequence[float]]
            One row per position.
        seed : int | None, optional
            The seed of the run, or None when it depends on no seed.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One series per output name.
        """
        columns = list(zip(*rows)) if rows else [() for _ in names]
        return cls(positions, dict(zip(names, columns, strict=True)), seed=seed)

    def rows(self) -> list[list[float]]:
        """
        Every output at each position, one row per position.

        Returns
        -------
        list[list[float]]
            ``rows()[i][j]`` is the value of the ``j``-th output, in key order
            (the order of ``Simulation.simulation_outputs``), at
            ``positions[i]``.
        """
        return [list(row) for row in zip(*self.values())] if self else []

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """The positions, the seed and the values."""
        seed = "" if self.seed is None else f"seed={self.seed!r}, "
        return (
            f"SimulationResults(positions={self.positions!r}, {seed}"
            f"{dict.__repr__(self)})"
        )
```

## ReplicateRuns

Runs replicates of a stochastic model; `Simulation.replicates` makes it.

Attributes:

| Name         | Type         | Description                                    |
| ------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `simulation` | `Simulation` | The simulation whose model the replicates run. |
| `n`          | `int`        | How many replicates.                           |
| `seed`       | `int`        | The seed the replicate seeds derive from.      |

Source code in `commol/api/simulation.py`

```python
class ReplicateRuns:
    """
    Runs replicates of a stochastic model; `Simulation.replicates` makes it.

    Attributes
    ----------
    simulation : Simulation
        The simulation whose model the replicates run.
    n : int
        How many replicates.
    seed : int
        The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
    """

    def __init__(self, simulation: Simulation, n: int, seed: int):
        """
        The replicates of a simulation.

        Parameters
        ----------
        simulation : Simulation
            The simulation whose model the replicates run.
        n : int
            How many replicates.
        seed : int
            The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
        """
        self.simulation = simulation
        self.n = n
        self.seed = seed

    def _replicates(
        self, num_steps: int | None, positions: list[float] | None
    ) -> SimulationReplicates:
        simulation = self.simulation
        simulation._validate_all_parameters_calibrated(simulation.model_definition)
        engine = simulation.engine
        grid, seeds, runs = engine.run_replicates(
            self.seed, self.n, num_steps=num_steps, positions=positions
        )
        outputs = simulation.simulation_outputs
        return SimulationReplicates(
            (
                SimulationResults.from_rows(grid, outputs, rows, seed=replicate_seed)
                for replicate_seed, rows in zip(seeds, runs, strict=True)
            ),
            seed=self.seed,
            positions=grid,
        )

    def run(self, num_steps: int) -> SimulationReplicates:
        """
        Every replicate from the initial state, on the default grid.

        Parameters
        ----------
        num_steps : int
            The number of steps: each replicate holds the positions
            ``0, 1, ..., num_steps``.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationReplicates
            One `SimulationResults` per replicate, each with its seed.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a replicate leaves the values the model allows.
        ValueError
            If a parameter or a value of the model has no value.
        """
        return self._replicates(num_steps, None)

    def run_at(self, at: Sequence[float]) -> SimulationReplicates:
        """
        Every replicate from the initial state, reported at given positions.

        Parameters
        ----------
        at : Sequence[float]
            Sorted, unique positions to report at.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationReplicates
            One `SimulationResults` per replicate, each with its seed.

        Raises
        ------
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a replicate leaves the values the model allows.
        ValueError
            If a parameter has no value, the positions are not sorted and
            unique, or the engine does not report at one of them.
        """
        return self._replicates(None, [float(position) for position in at])
```

## SimulationReplicates

Bases: `list[SimulationResults]`

Replicates of a run of a stochastic engine, one `SimulationResults` each.

A `list` of runs at the same positions, each with its own seed: `replicates[i].seed` repeats replicate `i`. The statistics reduce the replicates position by position, and `member_statistics` reduces them as `ci_percentiles` requires.

Attributes:

| Name        | Type          | Description                                       |
| ----------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `seed`      | `int`         | The seed the replicate seeds derive from.         |
| `positions` | `list[float]` | Positions on the axis, shared by every replicate. |

Source code in `commol/api/results.py`

```python
class SimulationReplicates(list[SimulationResults]):
    """
    Replicates of a run of a stochastic engine, one `SimulationResults` each.

    A ``list`` of runs at the same positions, each with its own seed:
    ``replicates[i].seed`` repeats replicate ``i``. The statistics reduce the
    replicates position by position, and `member_statistics` reduces them as
    ``ci_percentiles`` requires.

    Attributes
    ----------
    seed : int
        The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
    positions : list[float]
        Positions on the axis, shared by every replicate.
    """

    seed: int
    positions: list[float]

    def __init__(
        self, runs: Iterable[SimulationResults], seed: int, positions: Sequence[float]
    ):
        """
        Replicates of one run.

        Parameters
        ----------
        runs : Iterable[SimulationResults]
            One run per replicate, at `positions`.
        seed : int
            The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
        positions : Sequence[float]
            Positions on the axis, ascending.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a run is not at `positions`.
        """
        super().__init__(runs)
        self.seed = seed
        self.positions = [float(position) for position in positions]
        for index, run in enumerate(self):
            if run.positions != self.positions:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Replicate {index} is at other positions than the replicates."
                )

    @property
    def seeds(self) -> list[int]:
        """The seed of each replicate, in order."""
        return [run.seed for run in self if run.seed is not None]

    def _values(self, name: str) -> np.ndarray:
        if not self:
            raise ValueError("There are no replicates.")
        return np.asarray([run[name] for run in self], dtype=float)

    def mean(self) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        The mean of the replicates at each position, for each output.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One series of means per output, with no seed.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If there are no replicates.
        """
        names = list(self[0]) if self else []
        if not names:
            raise ValueError("There are no replicates.")
        return SimulationResults(
            self.positions,
            {name: self._values(name).mean(axis=0).tolist() for name in names},
        )

    def quantiles(self, levels: Sequence[float]) -> dict[float, SimulationResults]:
        """
        Quantiles of the replicates at each position, for each output.

        Parameters
        ----------
        levels : Sequence[float]
            Quantile levels, each between 0 and 1, such as ``[0.05, 0.5,
            0.95]``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[float, SimulationResults]
            The results of each level.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a level is outside ``[0, 1]`` or there are no replicates.
        """
        for level in levels:
            if not 0.0 <= level <= 1.0:
                raise ValueError(f"A quantile level is between 0 and 1, got {level}.")
        if not self:
            raise ValueError("There are no replicates.")
        names = list(self[0])
        return {
            level: SimulationResults(
                self.positions,
                {
                    name: np.quantile(self._values(name), level, axis=0).tolist()
                    for name in names
                },
            )
            for level in levels
        }

    def member_statistics(
        self, output: str, confidence_level: float
    ) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
        """
        The spread of one output across the replicates, at each position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        output : str
            An output name.
        confidence_level : float
            Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[float]]
            Keys ``mean``, ``median``, ``ci_lower``, ``ci_upper``, ``min`` and
            ``max``, one value per position (`member_statistics`).

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If no replicate has the output.
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is out of range or there are no
            replicates.
        """
        from commol.api.probabilistic.intervals import member_statistics

        if self and output not in self[0]:
            raise KeyError(
                f"'{output}' is not an output of the replicates. "
                f"Outputs: {sorted(self[0])}"
            )
        return member_statistics([run[output] for run in self], confidence_level)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """The number of replicates, their seed and their positions."""
        return (
            f"SimulationReplicates({len(self)} replicates, seed={self.seed!r}, "
            f"positions={self.positions!r})"
        )
```

```python
def quantiles(self, levels: Sequence[float]) -> dict[float, SimulationResults]:
    """
    Quantiles of the replicates at each position, for each output.

    Parameters
    ----------
    levels : Sequence[float]
        Quantile levels, each between 0 and 1, such as ``[0.05, 0.5,
        0.95]``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[float, SimulationResults]
        The results of each level.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a level is outside ``[0, 1]`` or there are no replicates.
    """
    for level in levels:
        if not 0.0 <= level <= 1.0:
            raise ValueError(f"A quantile level is between 0 and 1, got {level}.")
    if not self:
        raise ValueError("There are no replicates.")
    names = list(self[0])
    return {
        level: SimulationResults(
            self.positions,
            {
                name: np.quantile(self._values(name), level, axis=0).tolist()
                for name in names
            },
        )
        for level in levels
    }
```

#### member_statistics

```python
member_statistics(output: str, confidence_level: float) -> dict[str, list[float]]
```

The spread of one output across the replicates, at each position.

Parameters:

| Name               | Type    | Description                                                 | Default    |
| ------------------ | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `output`           | `str`   | An output name.                                             | *required* |
| `confidence_level` | `float` | Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1. | *required* |

Returns:

| Type                     | Description                                                                                     |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dict[str, list[float]]` | Keys mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min and max, one value per position (member_statistics). |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                         |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KeyError`   | If no replicate has the output.                                     |
| `ValueError` | If the confidence level is out of range or there are no replicates. |

Source code in `commol/api/results.py`

```python
def member_statistics(
    self, output: str, confidence_level: float
) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
    """
    The spread of one output across the replicates, at each position.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output : str
        An output name.
    confidence_level : float
        Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, list[float]]
        Keys ``mean``, ``median``, ``ci_lower``, ``ci_upper``, ``min`` and
        ``max``, one value per position (`member_statistics`).

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If no replicate has the output.
    ValueError
        If the confidence level is out of range or there are no
        replicates.
    """
    from commol.api.probabilistic.intervals import member_statistics

    if self and output not in self[0]:
        raise KeyError(
            f"'{output}' is not an output of the replicates. "
            f"Outputs: {sorted(self[0])}"
        )
    return member_statistics([run[output] for run in self], confidence_level)
```

```python
class StochasticEventsSettings(BaseModel):
    """
    Settings of the ``StochasticEvents`` engine.

    Attributes
    ----------
    method : Literal["direct", "tau_leaping"]
        ``"direct"``: Gillespie's direct method, one event at a time, exact.
        ``"tau_leaping"``: a Poisson number of events of each flow in each
        leap, an approximation that is faster when events are many.
    tau : float | None
        The length of a leap of ``"tau_leaping"``. None chooses each leap as
        Cao, Gillespie and Petzold (2006) do, from `epsilon`.
    epsilon : float
        How much a propensity may change in one chosen leap, relative to its
        value.
    tolerance : float
        Relative tolerance of the time of an event when a rate reads ``t``.
    rounding : Rounding | None
        How to make whole the initial amounts that are not. None requires
        whole amounts.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    method: Literal["direct", "tau_leaping"] = Field(
        default="direct", description="Simulation method."
    )
    tau: float | None = Field(
        default=None, gt=0.0, description="Length of a leap of tau-leaping."
    )
    epsilon: float = Field(
        default=0.03, gt=0.0, lt=1.0, description="Bound of an adaptive leap."
    )
    tolerance: float = Field(
        default=1e-8, gt=0.0, description="Relative tolerance of an event time."
    )
    rounding: Rounding | None = Field(
        default=None, description="How to make the initial amounts whole."
    )
```

## InfeasibleStateError

```python
InfeasibleStateError = _engine.InfeasibleStateError
```

A run left the values its model allows, such as an amount below zero.

A difference-equations step that leaves a compartment below zero raises it. It is a `ValueError`; a calibration treats such a run as infeasible.

## window_index

```python
window_index(at: float, window: float) -> int
```

Window a position belongs to.

The exact inverse of :func:`window_end`, and the containing window for any position in between: `max(ceil(at / window) - 1, 0)`. Position 0 belongs to window 0. :func:`commol.api.reporting.observed_report` places each observation with this rule.

| Type  | Description              |
| ----- | ------------------------ |
| `int` | Zero-based window index. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                  |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `ValueError` | If window is not positive or at is negative. |

Source code in `commol/api/windows.py`

```python
def window_index(at: float, window: float) -> int:
    """
    Window a position belongs to.

    The exact inverse of :func:`window_end`, and the containing window for
    any position in between: ``max(ceil(at / window) - 1, 0)``. Position 0
    belongs to window 0. :func:`commol.api.reporting.observed_report` places
    each observation with this rule.

    Parameters
    ----------
    at : float
        A position on the axis.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Zero-based window index.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive or `at` is negative.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    if not at >= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"at must not be negative, got {at}.")
    return max(math.ceil(_windows_in(at, window)) - 1, 0)
```

## window_ends

| Type          | Description                                                                   |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list[float]` | window, 2 * window, ... up to end. A trailing partial window is not included. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                |
| ------------ | -------------------------- |
| `ValueError` | If window is not positive. |

Source code in `commol/api/windows.py`

```python
def window_ends(window: float, end: float) -> list[float]:
    """
    Positions closing each complete window up to a position.

    Parameters
    ----------
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    end : float
        Last position covered, such as the last position of a run.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        ``window``, ``2 * window``, ... up to `end`. A trailing partial window
        is not included.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    count = math.floor(_windows_in(end, window)) if end > 0 else 0
    return [window_end(index, window) for index in range(count)]
```

## windowed_totals

```python
windowed_totals(series: Sequence[float], positions: Sequence[float], window: float, at: Iterable[float] | None = None) -> list[float]
```

Amount a cumulative series gained over each window.

Each value is the series at the end of the window minus the series at its start, `at - window`: the same quantity a calibration compares an observation against when that observation sets `window`.

Parameters:

| Name        | Type              | Description                                                              | Default                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `series`    | `Sequence[float]` | A cumulative series, one value per position.                             | *required*                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `positions` | `Sequence[float]` | Positions of the series, ascending, such as SimulationResults.positions. | *required*                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `window`    | `float`           | Length of one window on the axis.                                        | *required*                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `at`        | \`Iterable[float] | None\`                                                                   | Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete window of the series (:func:window_ends). Pass the observation positions to reproduce exactly the values a calibration used. |

Returns:

| Type          | Description                           |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `list[float]` | One increment per requested position. |

Raises:

| Type         | Description                                                                                                                             |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ValueError` | If window is not positive, a window starts before position 0, or the series has no value at the end or the start of a requested window. |

Source code in `commol/api/windows.py`

```python
def windowed_totals(
    series: Sequence[float],
    positions: Sequence[float],
    window: float,
    at: Iterable[float] | None = None,
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Amount a cumulative series gained over each window.

    Each value is the series at the end of the window minus the series at its
    start, ``at - window``: the same quantity a calibration compares an
    observation against when that observation sets ``window``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    series : Sequence[float]
        A cumulative series, one value per position.
    positions : Sequence[float]
        Positions of the series, ascending, such as
        ``SimulationResults.positions``.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    at : Iterable[float] | None, optional
        Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete window of
        the series (:func:`window_ends`). Pass the observation positions to
        reproduce exactly the values a calibration used.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One increment per requested position.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive, a window starts before position 0, or the
        series has no value at the end or the start of a requested window.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    ends = (
        window_ends(window, positions[-1] if positions else 0.0)
        if at is None
        else list(at)
    )

    totals = []
    for end in ends:
        start = end - window
        if start < -POSITION_TOLERANCE * max(abs(end), 1.0):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Position {end} has no complete window of {window} before it."
            )
        totals.append(
            series[index_at(positions, end)]
            - series[index_at(positions, max(start, 0.0))]
        )
    return totals
```

# Model Structure

[Back to API Reference](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/index.md)

A `Model` is a tree of Pydantic models. `ModelBuilder` creates it, `Model.to_json` writes it, and the Rust engine reads the same tree from JSON (`crates/commol-core/src/types/`). Most users never build these types by hand; read this page to understand model files or to work on Commol.

A model has a header, a **process** written once, a **structure** that lays the process out, and an **engine** that runs it. The process (bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions) is the same for every kind of model; the structure changes between kinds and is tagged in JSON by `kind`, and by `variant` for a narrower form of a structure. The kind today is `aggregate`: amounts per compartment.

```text
Model                      name, description, version, step_unit
├── parameters: [Parameter]                (a value may be a SeriesValue)
├── engine: ModelEngine
│   ├── type: "DifferenceEquations", "DifferentialEquations",
│   │         "StochasticEvents" or "StochasticSteps"
│   └── settings: OdeSolver | StochasticEventsSettings | StochasticStepsSettings | None
│                                           (settings of that engine; None: its defaults)
├── process: Process
│   ├── bins: [Bin]
│   ├── accumulators: [Accumulator]
│   ├── stratifications: [Stratification]
│   │   └── conditions: [StratificationCondition]
│   └── transitions: [Transition]          (impulse_at, impulse_every for impulses)
│       └── stratified_rates: [StratifiedRate]
│           └── conditions: [StratificationCondition]
└── structure: Aggregate                   (kind: "aggregate", variant: None)
    ├── total: float
    ├── bin_fractions: {bin: fraction | None}
    ├── stratification_fractions: {stratification: {category: fraction}}
    ├── compartment_fractions: {compartment: fraction}
    └── neighbors: Complete | Groups | None
```

In JSON the structure is an object with its `kind`, its `variant` and the fields of its class:

```json
{
  "name": "Model",
  "parameters": [],
  "engine": {"type": "DifferenceEquations", "settings": null},
  "process": {"bins": [], "accumulators": [], "stratifications": [], "transitions": []},
  "structure": {
    "kind": "aggregate",
    "variant": null,
    "total": 1000.0,
    "bin_fractions": {"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01},
    "stratification_fractions": {},
    "compartment_fractions": {},
    "neighbors": null
  },
  "step_unit": null
}
```

`Model`, `Process`, `ModelStructure`, `Aggregate`, `Complete` and `Groups` are documented in [Model API](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/api/model/index.md). The engine must run the kind of the structure: a model whose engine runs another kind is rejected when it is made, with an error that names the engine, both kinds and the engines of the kind of the model. A variant keeps the kind, the fields and the engines of its structure, and loads back as its own class ([Design decisions](https://munqu.github.io/commol/latest/codebase/design-decisions/#a-model-is-a-header-a-process-a-structure-and-an-engine)).

```python
class Bin(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a single bin (base category) of the process of a model.

    A bin represents a fundamental category before stratification. The combination
    of a bin with all stratifications produces the actual compartments.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Identifier of the bin.
    name : str
        A descriptive, human-readable name for the bin.
    unit : str | None
        The unit of measurement for this bin.
        If None, the bin will use the model-level bin_unit when specified.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(..., description="Identifier of the bin.")
    name: str = Field(..., description="Descriptive, human-readable name for the bin.")
    unit: str | None = Field(
        None,
        description="Unit of measurement for this bin.",
    )

    @override
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash(self.id)

    @override
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return isinstance(other, Bin) and self.id == other.id
```

## Stratifications

## Stratification

Bases: `BaseModel`

Defines a categorical subdivision of the compartments.

Attributes:

| Name          | Type                            | Description                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`          | `str`                           | Identifier of the stratification.                        |
| `categories`  | `list[str]`                     | List of the different stratification groups identifiers. |
| `description` | \`str                           | None\`                                                   |
| `conditions`  | \`list[StratificationCondition] | None\`                                                   |

Source code in `commol/context/stratification.py`

```python
class Stratification(BaseModel):
    """
    Defines a categorical subdivision of the compartments.

    Attributes
    ----------
    id : str
        Identifier of the stratification.
    categories : list[str]
        List of the different stratification groups identifiers.
    description : str | None
        A human-readable description of the stratification.
    conditions : list[StratificationCondition] | None
        When set, this stratification only expands compartments whose
        already-applied stratification categories satisfy ALL conditions.
        Compartments that do not satisfy the conditions are kept without
        appending this stratification's categories.

        May only reference stratifications declared before this one.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    id: str = Field(default=..., description="Identifier of the stratification.")
    categories: list[str] = Field(
        default=...,
        description="List of the different stratification groups identifiers.",
    )
    description: str | None = Field(
        default=None, description="Human-readable description of the stratification."
    )
    conditions: list[StratificationCondition] | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Conditions on previously-declared stratifications that must be "
            "satisfied for this stratification to expand a compartment."
        ),
    )

    @override
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash(self.id)

    @override
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        return isinstance(other, Stratification) and self.id == other.id

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_categories_length(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that categories are not empty.
        """
        if not self.categories:
            raise ValueError(
                (f"Stratification '{self.id}' must have at least one category.")
            )
        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_categories_uniqueness(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that categories are not repeated.
        """
        categories_set = set(self.categories)

        if len(categories_set) != len(self.categories):
            duplicates = [
                item for item in categories_set if self.categories.count(item) > 1
            ]
            raise ValueError(
                (
                    f"Categories for stratification '{self.id}' must not be repeated. "
                    f"Found duplicates: {list(set(duplicates))}."
                )
            )

        return self

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_conditions_have_categories(self) -> Self:
        """
        Enforces that stratification expansion conditions filter by category.
        """
        if self.conditions is None:
            return self

        for condition in self.conditions:
            if condition.category is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    (
                        f"Condition for stratification '{self.id}' referencing "
                        f"'{condition.stratification}' must include a category. "
                        "Category-less conditions are only valid for transition "
                        "target overrides."
                    )
                )

        return self
```
